ES=F close · close 7,267.25

-1 neutral

ES=F closed 7267.25 on 23 November (from 6966.75, +4.31%) as the S&P 500 cash index rose 4.73% (+326.78) to 7,237.17, its best day since April 2025, recovering most of Friday's 3.70% fall and the bulk of the prior week's 8.57-8.61% decline (CappNotes Closing Look, 23 November). The Dow rose 3.01% (+1,447.98) to 49,595.31 and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51% (+1,471.83) to 24,089.56, its best day since 9 April 2025. The trigger was single-stock: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive about two weeks after he resigned, saying it had received input from senior US government levels, and President Trump said he had 'convinced' the board; NVDA rose 31.48%, its best day since 2003, taking its market value to roughly $4 trillion from about $3 trillion at Friday's close (CNBC and Fortune, 23 November). Breadth inverted from Friday: 417 advancers to 83 decliners with 10 of 11 sectors higher - Technology +8.97%, Consumer Discretionary +3.97%, Industrials +3.90% against Consumer Staples -0.09% and Energy -1.06% - but equal-weight RSP rose only 2.59%, 214bp less than the cap-weighted index, so the recovery was as concentrated as the decline was. VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62 from 35.89. Treasuries barely moved: the 2-year unchanged at 4.63%, the 10-year unchanged at 4.92% (bondstats has it 2.2bp lower at 4.9218% on the New York close), the 30-year about 2bp lower at 5.29%, 2s10s about 29bp. Credit joined the rally, HYG +0.25%, JNK +0.28% and LQD +0.23%, though the ICE BofA high-yield spread's latest dated print is 3.76% as of 20 November, up from 3.52%. CME FedWatch put a 25bp hike at the 9 December FOMC at about 98%, with 50bp largely priced out. S&P Global's flash November PMIs missed: composite 54.6 from 55.9, the slowest private-sector expansion in four months, services 54.7 against 55.6-55.7 expected and manufacturing 54.5 from 54.9. WTI fell 3.88% to $80.17, its lowest close since 26 August, on Russia-Ukraine peace-deal progress. RSI 41.40, with the close 5.1% below the 50-day (7656.12) and 1.5% below the 200-day (7379.22); 1H structure choppy, weekly structure uptrend.written Tue Nov 24, 9:45 AM ET · data through Mon Nov 23 close

10-Year Treasury Note

ZN=F close · close 106.61

+0 neutral

ZN=F closed 106.609375 on 23 November - to the tick the same price it closed on 20 November, a 0.00% session, the flattest print in this ledger's record - as the equity rout reversed without moving the curve: the 2-year unchanged at 4.63%, the 10-year unchanged at 4.92% (bondstats reports it 2.2bp lower at 4.9218% on the New York close and describes yields as 'little changed'), the 30-year about 2bp lower at 5.29% and 2s10s about 29bp (CappNotes Closing Look, 23 November; bondstats daily, 23 November). That the note held its five-session haven gain on a day the S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the VIX fell 25.83% is the session's one real Treasury fact. Credit cut both ways: HYG +0.25% and JNK +0.28% against LQD +0.23%, so junk marginally outperformed duration on the day, while the ICE BofA high-yield spread's latest dated print is 3.76% as of 20 November, up from 3.52% on the 19th and 3.47% on the 18th - a 29bp widening across three dated prints. NQ=F closed 26829.0 on 23 November (from 25291.0, +6.08%) as the Nasdaq-100 cash index rose 6.86% (+1,717.12) to 26,746.10 and the Composite 6.51% (+1,471.83) to 24,089.56, its best day since 9 April 2025 (CappNotes Closing Look, 23 November). The whole move traces to one governance event: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive about two weeks after he resigned, saying it had received input from senior US government levels, with President Trump saying he had 'convinced' the board; NVDA rose 31.48%, its best day since 2003, taking its market value to roughly $4 trillion from about $3 trillion at Friday's close, and Melius upgraded to buy at a $220 target and Bernstein to outperform at $200 the same day (CNBC and Fortune, 23 November). Technology led all 11 S&P 500 sectors at +8.97% and nine of the ten largest gainers on the day were semis or AI-infrastructure names: ALAB +23.16%, CRWV +22.32%, SITM +21.48%, MXL +21.38%, DELL +20.46%, NBIS +20.28%, MU +19.04%, SMTC +18.83%, MTSI +18.67%. The leadership was narrow by construction: equal-weight RSP rose 2.59% against the Nasdaq-100's 6.86%, a 427bp gap. Cutting the other way, CrowdStrike fell 8.92%, the worst performer in the S&P 500, on its all-stock offer for Zscaler valued at about $43.9 billion - the largest cybersecurity takeover on record, 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share for roughly $260.41, a ~34% premium, with CRWD holders to own about 84% of the combined company (CrowdStrike press release, 23 November). Overseas, Korea's finance ministry prepared a market stabilisation fund of more than 10 trillion won, its first since 2008, Taiwan's regulator tightened short-selling rules and Chinese exchanges eased margin financing; Taiwan's Taiex rose 2.2-2.4% and the Stoxx 600 0.8%, while the Kospi still fell about 3.3% (news log, 23 November). VXN fell to 36.31 from 45.25. Yields were unchanged (2-year 4.63%, 10-year 4.92%), which matters because the Nasdaq-100's two dominant 21-session drivers are the 10-year at corr +0.442 and oil at -0.400, and WTI fell 3.88% to $80.17.   • Cross-asset · Nov 24 9:45amOil at corr -0.400 is one of two dominant measured drivers and it fell 3.88% to $80.17, its lowest close since 26 August, with Brent -3.46%. Behind it, the official support measures that landed on S are aimed squarely at this index's supply chain: Korea's finance ministry preparing a stabilisation fund of more than 10 trillion won, its first since 2008, Taiwan tightening short-selling rules and Chinese exchanges easing margin financing, with Taiwan's Taiex up 2.2-2.4% on TSMC and MediaTek (news log, 23 November). A 5-session tailwind, even with the Kospi still down about 3.3% on the day.
  • Market structure (HH/HL) · Nov 24 9:45amWeekly structure is choppy - no consistent run of higher or lower swings.
